note: The third corpus (construct-4jq), and the one that shows what the first two cannot. labeled-outcomes.json was written alongside the catalog and scores 0.000. held-out-outcomes.json was written to escape that circularity and scored 0.632 before construct-gsf tuned the catalog until it reached 0.026 — at which point it stopped being held out. These ten were authored during the construct-r67.9 dogfood, situation-first and before reading the keyword lists in that session, and scored 0.400 against a 0.15 target on a catalog that scored 0.026 on the corpus it had been tuned against. The gap between 0.026 and 0.400 is the tuning, not the map.
status: BURNED. Writing this file down is what spends it: from here on the catalog can be tuned against these ten, so passing them proves progressively less. It is committed anyway, because a regression against it is still real information and an uncommitted measurement is not a gate. Its miss rate is recorded as a fact to be watched, NOT enforced as a passing threshold — enforcing it would be the exact instruction to tune against it.
discipline: Same rule as held-out-outcomes.json: state the situation first, then write it in the plainest words available; never reach for a term because the catalog contains it; never reword a failing case until it passes. `expect` is what a competent human would say the outcome implicates, decided at authoring time and not revised after seeing the matcher's answer.
howToExtend: Do not extend this file. A generalization measurement is only worth what its wording cost, and appending to a corpus the catalog has already been tuned against buys nothing. Author a NEW file of never-seen wording, measure once, then commit it in this same burned state with its number recorded. The measurement that matters is always the next unspent one.
